goal: A React Native Reusables port of Vercel's AI Elements — universal iOS, Android and Web AI chat and agent UI, distributed as a copy-paste registry.
vibe: Match React Native Reusables for all shared vocabulary — radius, spacing rhythm, type ramp, borders, press states, motion durations — while genuinely new AI surfaces (streaming shimmer, tool status badges, reasoning trace) carry their own visual treatment so an agent action reads as distinct from ordinary app chrome. Distinctness comes from composition and existing roles only; the library declares no new tokens.

build_plan.scope_rule: Components that map directly to AI Elements. Nothing duplicating RNR. Nothing a consumer cannot install.
build_plan.tokens: SKIP — the library declares none; consuming RNR's is the promise
build_plan.cut_correction: sidebar and toaster were in the atom list on FALSE POSITIVES from the derivation: 'sidebar' matched the word context in 'a SidebarProvider context', and 'toaster' matched 'queue' in 'a module-level queue store'. Neither is a component reference, and no in-scope component lists either as a dependency. toaster also had nothing to host, since toast was already cut. Atoms 12 -> 10, total 55 -> 53.
build_plan.canvas_family_correction: controls, toolbar and panel moved OUT OF SCOPE. The product lens read them as a generic media transport, an icon row and a split pane. The web-original lens — the authority on what the web component IS — says controls is React Flow's zoom cluster acting on its viewport store, toolbar is @xyflow/react NodeToolbar positioned from the owning node's measured DOM rect inside a nodeTypes component, and panel is an absolutely positioned View inside the transform layer. All three verdict 'drop'. canvas/node/edge/connection are already out of scope, so their satellites cannot function. Molecules 9 -> 6, total 53 -> 50, out-of-scope 6 -> 9.
build_plan.persona_note: persona is Rive (WebGL2 on web; rive-react-native natively), NOT the avatar card the product lens described. Shipped here as the identity card WITHOUT the animated avatar, which keeps the registry dependency-free; the Rive runtime would be an opt-in item if ever wanted.

wave_2.evidence: iOS simulator: Base Primitives/Item Rows renders outline + muted + plain rows, Icon via RNR's wrapper, TextClassContext differentiating title from description. All four bundle (4484 modules). Contract passes on 5 registry sources.
wave_2.note: sheet mounts its own NAMED PortalHost (useSheetPortalHost) — without it any RNR overlay opened inside renders BEHIND the sheet, silently, on device only.

wave_3.evidence: iOS simulator: AI Elements/Chat/Populated renders a real chat — user bubble on bg-primary right-aligned, assistant full-width with avatar, code-block with filename header + copy + line-number gutter, composer with send button. Content sits at the BOTTOM of the viewport, which is the inverted FlatList reproducing the web original's grow-from-bottom.

key_decisions.conversation: Inverted FlatList + maintainVisibleContentPosition. Stick-to-bottom is free (offset 0 IS the bottom) and releases the moment the user scrolls up, never taken back. Virtualized from day one — the prior RN port shipped ScrollView + .map().
key_decisions.message: prop is `from` not `role` (the documented most-common port error). Markdown INJECTED via renderMarkdown, default plain Text — that seam keeps the core Expo Go-clean.
key_decisions.prompt-input: Explicit send button is the ONLY submit path; the web Enter/Shift+Enter/IME contract is meaningless on a soft keyboard. A REJECTED onSubmit leaves the text intact.
key_decisions.code-block: Unhighlighted MVP; chrome 100% RNR. Horizontal scroll, no wrap. Copy flips 2000ms and reports failure.

wave_5.evidence: iOS simulator: AI Elements/Molecules/Streaming Shimmer captured mid-pulse — two active rows faded at reduced opacity while active={false} sits at full text-muted-foreground. 4515 modules bundle.
wave_5.scope_correction: controls, toolbar and panel moved OUT OF SCOPE as canvas-family. The web-original lens (authority on what the web component IS) verdicts all three 'drop': controls is React Flow's zoom cluster on its viewport store, toolbar is @xyflow/react NodeToolbar positioned from a node's measured DOM rect, panel is a positioned View inside the transform layer. The product lens had misread them as a media transport, an icon row and a split pane. canvas/node/edge/connection are already out of scope, so their satellites cannot function. Molecules 9 -> 6, total 53 -> 50.
wave_5.persona_divergence: The web persona is a Rive animation (WebGL2 on web, rive-react-native natively), not the avatar card the product lens described. Shipped as the identity surface WITHOUT the animated avatar, so no consumer inherits a native animation runtime for a component most use as a header. Recorded as a real gap in the verdict table rather than implied parity.
wave_5.shimmer_note: The only genuinely invented treatment in the port. React Native has no background-clip:text, so it reuses RNR Skeleton's exact motion signature (opacity 1->0.5, 1000ms, withRepeat reverse) rather than the web's 2000ms gradient sweep — an invented treatment that borrows the house pulse reads as house style. Gated on useReducedMotion, where RNR's own Skeleton is not.
wave_5.speech_input_note: Ships the web original's caller-supplied-transcriber contract as the ONLY contract, so no speech dependency enters anyone's install graph. Disabled with no engine wired (never fake-listening); only final non-empty transcripts fire; permission-denied is a distinct state because on mobile capability != permission.

notes.dual_engine: The registry emits BOTH nativewind and uniwind variants at 32/32 parity, mirroring RNR. Measured basis: RNR's own two variants differ only by an import-path segment and formatting — 125 identical class tokens, zero nativewind-only classes, and the only two uniwind-only classes live in icon.tsx, which we consume from RNR rather than write. Our source stays engine-agnostic; the build fans it out by rewriting the alias segment and the registryDependencies URL segment.
notes.harness_engine: Storybook runs on ONE engine (uniwind) because a sandbox needs a single bundler. The nativewind variant is validated by CI installing it into a clean Expo app and typechecking, which is proportionate given the emitted delta is an import path.
notes.customization: Consumers get RNR's own customization contract unchanged: the library declares no tokens (verified — RNR registry items ship no cssVars and no theme.ts), and components ride cn + cva + TextClassContext through the consumer's aliases. A consumer on either RNR setup is supported.

notes.scaffold_gate: Deliberately still PENDING. The workflow's step 9 requires the sandbox to run and token stories to render; Storybook is not installed yet. The workspace, theme, all 32 RNR components, PortalHost and a hello-world are done and verified (0 tsc errors, real Metro bundle). Marking the gate passed before Storybook exists would be fake success.
notes.pin_corrections: Three corrections verified against sources, not inferred: react-native is 0.86.3 (Expo 57's pin, confirmed by Expo's own scaffolder) not 0.87.1; @react-native-reusables/cli is 1.0.0 not 0.7.1; Expo 57's template pins typescript ~6.0.3 while AGENTS.md/PRD say 7.0.2 — harness runs 6.0.3, workspace root holds 7.0.2.
notes.cli_findings: RNR's `init` is interactive and cannot be scripted (hangs on a TTY prompt with piped stdin). `add` works non-interactively with --yes --all --overwrite --styling-library. components.json REQUIRES aliases.utils — omitting it fails validation with 'Invalid components.json'. RNR's doctor asks for tailwindcss-animate even on the uniwind path, which is a Tailwind v3 plugin the styling contract forbids in the uniwind emit.
notes.hoisting_correction: node-linker=hoisted was REMOVED. It was added on the assumption that pnpm's symlinks trip Metro; that assumption was wrong for Expo 57 / Metro, and hoisting actively broke dual-engine support by flattening nativewind into the root where it resolved tailwindcss@4 instead of its package-local v3. With pnpm's default isolated linker, apps/harness resolves tailwindcss 4.3.3 and apps/harness-nativewind resolves 3.4.19, and both engines build.
notes.engine_toggle: The Storybook Engine toolbar item cannot hot-swap engines — both are bundler transforms and NativeWind 4 requires Tailwind v3 while Uniwind requires v4. It reports the running engine and hard-refreshes to the other server, which is why each engine has its own workspace package and port.
notes.rtk_warning: `rtk` wraps tsc and reported 'TypeScript: No errors found' on a run that exited 1 with a real TS2688 error. Verify gates with the direct binary when an exit code and the printed output disagree.
notes.sandbox_scope: The sandbox contains ONLY components this library ships. RNR already exports tokens and Button, and consumers get those from RNR directly, so re-storying them here would duplicate RNR and demo nothing installable. The scaffold smoke stories (RNR Button, design tokens) were deleted once they had done their job of proving the pipeline; their evidence is recorded above.
